note: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/RecSim NG- Toward Principled Uncertainty Modeling for Recommender Ecosystems.md

primary_source.coverage: Read the extracted paper sequentially from title/abstract through §§1–5, including all formal DBN equations and code examples, behavioral-library descriptions, runtime and inference/learning APIs, all three use cases, conclusions, and all bibliography entries. Checked note abstract, model claims and footnotes against source passages; checked metadata and source version. Guides LLM Extraction Rules, Model Notation, and paper Template were consulted. The paper refers detailed tutorial model values/specifications externally; did not infer them.

claim_checks.claim: Abstract characterizes RecSim NG as a probabilistic, scalable/modular/differentiable multi-agent recommender simulator implemented in Edward2 and TensorFlow with inference/latent learning and accelerated runtime support.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note abstract matches source abstract wording and substance.

claim_checks.claim: State/process schema factors a Markov state into component variables, initial distributions and transition factors conditioned on current- and previous-slice parents; runtime observability differs from each agent's observation subset.
claim_checks.result: PASS; schema and description preserve both dependency types and partial observability distinction.
claim_checks.source_location: §3.1, DBN transition factorization and runtime-observability discussion.

claim_checks.claim: Entities encapsulate batched population parameters/behaviors; stories instantiate and bind variables and behavior dependencies; choice/state libraries include the listed families.
claim_checks.result: PASS; correctly presented as architecture/library abstractions rather than universal behavior.

claim_checks.claim: Specific §3.3 user example initializes unit-normal interests, chooses by softmax/MNL weights proportional to exp of negative Euclidean feature distance, observes quality on consumption, and updates interest by sensitivity times quality-weighted feature displacement plus Gaussian noise.
claim_checks.result: PASS on model rule, choice and update order; schema explicitly scopes it to the §3.3 illustration. ACTION: note says 'Noise covariance, sensitivity and recommendation slates are configuration inputs.' The paper specifies Gaussian noise and a sensitivity parameter, but does not supply/configure a covariance value or characterize covariance as an input. Rephrase as unspecified noise covariance/parameters or cite an actual supplied configuration; tutorials are outside this source.

claim_checks.claim: §4.1 partially observable RL use case uses finite 15-consumed-item history, learned belief/embeddings, REINFORCE, slate size 2, dimension 20, 1,000 users, horizon 100 and 20-run figure average.
claim_checks.result: PASS; stated controls match paper. The note properly avoids inventing optimizer/initialization settings not reported there.

claim_checks.claim: §4.2 learning use case has static interests, dynamic satisfaction based on adjacent-slate best-affinity trend, per-user latent sensitivity, randomized data-generation recommender, and HMC within Monte Carlo EM; learning sensitivity initialized Uniform(0,1).
claim_checks.result: PASS; scope and non-reproduced tutorial details are disclosed.

claim_checks.claim: §4.3 ecosystem example describes static observable user interests, provider/user community mixtures, discounted engagement-dependent provider item generation, comparison of myopic and capped boost policies, and reported utility controls/outcomes.
claim_checks.result: PASS; 2,000 users, 80 providers, 400 items/period, horizon 300, 40 runs, L=1.2 utility 161.34 vs 130.77, and approximately 6x TPUv2 speedup are source-supported. The opposite-signed boost prose is accurately retained as unresolved source tension.

claim_checks.claim: Capabilities and use scope include trajectory simulation, log-probability evaluation, gradient-based fitting, posterior inference/latent learning, policy-gradient and other inference/training uses.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note makes no unsupported claim of performance guarantee or empirical validation beyond the cited use cases.
